verses.zh: 我的弟兄们，你们信奉我们荣耀的主耶稣基督，便不可按着外貌待人。
verses.en: My brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] do not show prejudice[NOTE:2] if you possess faith[NOTE:3] in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:2.
Or “partiality.”
Grk “do not have faith with personal prejudice,” with emphasis on the last phrase.
Grk “our Lord Jesus Christ of glory.” Here δόξης (doxēs) has been translated as an attributive genitive.

verses.zh: 若有一个人带着金戒指，穿着华美衣服，进你们的会堂去；又有一个穷人穿着肮脏衣服也进去；
verses.en: For if someone[NOTE:1] comes into your assembly[NOTE:2] wearing a gold ring and fine clothing, and a poor person enters in filthy clothes,
notes: The word for “man” or “individual” here is ἀνήρ (anēr), which often means “male” or “man (as opposed to woman).” But as BDAG 79 s.v. 2 says, “equivalent to τὶς someone.”

Grk “synagogue.” Usually συναγωγή refers to Jewish places of worship (e.g., Matt 4:23, Mark 1:21, Luke 4:15, John 6:59). The word can be used generally to refer to a place of assembly, and here it refers specifically to a Christian assembly (BDAG 963 s.v. 2.b.).

verses.zh: 你们就重看那穿华美衣服的人，说：「请坐在这好位上」；又对那穷人说：「你站在那里」，或「坐在我脚凳下边。」
verses.en: do you pay attention to the one who is finely dressed and say,[NOTE:1] “You sit here in a good place,”[NOTE:2] and to the poor person, “You stand over there,” or “Sit on the floor”?[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “and you pay attention…and say,” continuing the “if” clauses from v. 2. In the Greek text, vv. 2-4 form one long sentence.
Or “sit here, please.”

Grk “sit under my footstool.” The words “on the floor” have been supplied in the translation to clarify for the modern reader the undesirability of this seating arrangement (so also TEV, NIV, CEV, NLT). Another option followed by a number of translations is to replace “under my footstool” with “at my feet” (NAB, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 这岂不是你们偏心待人，用恶意断定人吗？
verses.en: If so, have you not made distinctions[NOTE:1] among yourselves and become judges with evil motives?[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “have you not made distinctions” (as the conclusion to the series of “if” clauses in vv. 2-3).
Grk “judges of evil reasonings.”

verses.zh: 我亲爱的弟兄们，请听，　神岂不是拣选了世上的贫穷人，叫他们在信上富足，并承受他所应许给那些爱他之人的国吗？
verses.en: Listen, my dear brothers and sisters![NOTE:1] Did not God choose the poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom that he promised to those who love him?
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:2.

verses.zh: 你们反倒羞辱贫穷人。那富足人岂不是欺压你们、拉你们到公堂去吗？
verses.en: But you have dishonored the poor![NOTE:1] Are not the rich oppressing you and dragging you into the courts?
notes: This is singular: “the poor person,” perhaps referring to the hypothetical one described in vv. 2-3.

verses.zh: 他们不是亵渎你们所敬奉（所敬奉：或译被称）的尊名吗？
verses.en: Do they not blaspheme the good name of the one you belong to?[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “that was invoked over you,” referring to their baptism in which they confessed their faith in Christ and were pronounced to be his own. To have the Lord’s name “named over them” is OT imagery for the Lord’s ownership of his people (cf. 2 Chr 7:14; Amos 9:12; Isa 63:19; Jer 14:9; 15:16; Dan 9:19; Acts 15:17).

verses.zh: 经上记着说：「要爱人如己。」你们若全守这至尊的律法才是好的。
verses.en: But if you fulfill the royal law as expressed in this scripture,[NOTE:1] “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,”[NOTE:2] you are doing well.
notes: Grk “according to the scripture.”
A quotation from Lev 19:18 (also quoted in Matt 19:19; 22:39; Mark 12:31; Luke 10:27; Rom 13:9; Gal 5:14).

verses.zh: 但你们若按外貌待人，便是犯罪，被律法定为犯法的。
verses.en: But if you show prejudice, you are committing sin and are convicted by the law as violators.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “transgressors.”

verses.zh: 因为凡遵守全律法的，只在一条上跌倒，他就是犯了众条。
verses.en: For the one who obeys the whole law but fails[NOTE:1] in one point has become guilty of all of it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “stumbles.”
Grk “guilty of all.”

verses.zh: 原来那说「不可奸淫」的，也说「不可杀人」；你就是不奸淫，却杀人，仍是成了犯律法的。
verses.en: For he who said, “Do not commit adultery,”[NOTE:1] also said, “Do not murder.”[NOTE:2] Now if you do not commit adultery but do commit murder, you have become a violator of the law.
notes: A quotation from Exod 20:14 and Deut 5:18.
A quotation from Exod 20:13 and Deut 5:17.

verses.zh: 你们既然要按使人自由的律法受审判，就该照这律法说话行事。
verses.en: Speak and act as those who will be judged by a law that gives freedom.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “a law of freedom.”

verses.zh: 因为那不怜悯人的，也要受无怜悯的审判；怜悯原是向审判夸胜。
verses.en: For judgment is merciless for the one who has shown no mercy. But mercy triumphs over[NOTE:1] judgment.
notes: Grk “boasts against, exults over,” in victory.

verses.zh: 我的弟兄们，若有人说自己有信心，却没有行为，有甚么益处呢？这信心能救他吗？
verses.en: What good is it, my brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] if someone claims to have faith but does not have works? Can this kind of faith[NOTE:2] save him?[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:2.

Grk “the faith,” referring to the kind of faith just described: faith without works. The article here is anaphoric, referring to the previous mention of the noun πίστις (pistis) in the verse. See ExSyn 219.
The form of the question in Greek expects a negative answer.

verses.zh: 若是弟兄或是姊妹，赤身露体，又缺了日用的饮食；
verses.en: If a brother or sister[NOTE:1] is poorly clothed and lacks daily food,
notes: It is important to note that the words ἀδελφός (adelphos) and ἀδελφή (adelphē) both occur in the Greek text at this point, confirming that the author intended to refer to both men and women. See the note on “someone” in 2:2.

verses.zh: 你们中间有人对他们说：「平平安安地去吧！愿你们穿得暖，吃得饱」，却不给他们身体所需用的，这有甚么益处呢？
verses.en: and one of you says to them, “Go in peace, keep warm and eat well,” but you do not give them what the body needs,[NOTE:1] what good is it?
notes: Grk “what is necessary for the body.”

verses.zh: 这样，信心若没有行为就是死的。
verses.en: So also faith, if it does not have works, is dead being by itself.

verses.zh: 必有人说：「你有信心，我有行为；你将你没有行为的信心指给我看，我便藉着我的行为，将我的信心指给你看。」
verses.en: But someone will say, “You have faith and I have works.”[NOTE:1] Show me your faith without works and I will show you faith by[NOTE:2] my works.
notes: There is considerable doubt about where the words of the “someone” end and where James’ reply begins. Some see the quotation running to the end of v. 18; others to the end of v. 19. But most punctuate as shown above. The “someone” is then an objector, and the sense of his words is something like, “Some have faith; others have works; don’t expect everyone to have both.” James’ reply is that faith cannot exist or be seen without works.
Or “from.”

verses.zh: 你信　神只有一位，你信的不错；鬼魔也信，却是战惊。
verses.en: You believe that God is one; well and good.[NOTE:1] Even the demons believe that—and tremble with fear.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “you do well.”
Grk “believe and tremble.” The words “with fear” are implied.

verses.zh: 虚浮的人哪，你愿意知道没有行为的信心是死的吗？
verses.en: But would you like evidence,[NOTE:1] you empty fellow,[NOTE:2] that faith without works is useless?[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “do you want to know.”

Grk “O empty man.” Here the singular vocative ἄνθρωπε (anthrōpe, “man”) means “person” or even “fellow.” Cf. BDAG 82 s.v. ἄνθρωπος 8 which views this as an instance of rhetorical address in a letter; the pejorative sense is also discussed under the previous heading (7).

Most witnesses, including several significant ones (א A C2 P Ψ 5 33 81 436 442 1611 1735 1852 2344 2492 M al sy bo), have νεκρά (nekra, “dead”) here, while P74 reads κενή (kenē, “empty”). Both variants are most likely secondary, derived from ἀργή (argē, “useless”). The reading of the majority is probably an assimilation to the statements in vv. 17 and 26, while P74’s reading picks up on κενέ (kene) earlier in the verse. The external evidence (B C* 323 945 1175 1243 1739 sa) for ἀργή is sufficient for authenticity; coupled with the strong internal evidence for the reading (if νεκρά were original, how would ἀργή have arisen here and not in vv. 17 or 26?), it is strongly preferred.

verses.zh: 我们的祖宗亚伯拉罕把他儿子以撒献在坛上，岂不是因行为称义吗？
verses.en: Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered Isaac his son on the altar?

verses.zh: 可见，信心是与他的行为并行，而且信心因着行为才得成全。
verses.en: You see that his faith was working together with his works and his faith was perfected by works.

verses.zh: 这就应验经上所说：「亚伯拉罕信　神，这就算为他的义。」他又得称为　神的朋友。
verses.en: And the scripture was fulfilled that says, “Now Abraham believed God and it was counted to him for righteousness,”[NOTE:1] and he was called God’s friend.[NOTE:2]
notes: A quotation from Gen 15:6.
An allusion to 2 Chr 20:7; Isa 41:8; 51:2; Dan 3:35 (LXX), in which Abraham is called God’s “beloved.”

verses.zh: 这样看来，人称义是因着行为，不是单因着信。
verses.en: You see that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone.

verses.zh: 妓女喇合接待使者，又放他们从别的路上出去，不也是一样因行为称义吗？
verses.en: And similarly, was not Rahab the prostitute also justified by works when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another way?

verses.zh: 身体没有灵魂是死的，信心没有行为也是死的。
verses.en: For just as the body without the spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.
